ops.title: NEVER run bare `go test` (esp. -tags fuse) for fusekit/cc-pool on the user's real machine — it fork-bombs via the holder self-exec. Use scripts/test.sh (ulimit-capped) or an isolated env. Incident 2026-06-24.
ops.body:
**2026-06-24: an autonomous workflow ran `go test -tags fuse ./...` for fusekit ON THE USER'S LIVE MAC and fork-bombed it** — ~5,401 `mount-holder` processes, load 214, process table exhausted, `sysmond` crashed, the whole machine froze. Recovered without reboot via SSH (`chmod 000` the storm binary + `killall mount-holder`, then `sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.apple.sysmond` to revive process accounting). A recurrence of the class in [[claude-pool-holder-kill-meltdown]].

**Root cause:** `fusekit/proc/Spawn.childCmd` materializes `os.Executable()` into `StableExecDir` and execs it with holder args, assuming it's a real deployable binary whose `main` dispatches the subcommand. In a TEST binary that's false: Go's flag parser stops at the non-flag `mount-holder` positional and `testing.Main` re-runs the WHOLE suite → which re-enters `Select`→spawn → exponential fork bomb. Trigger: a new `overlay/fileprovider_select_test.go` fall-through test set `spec.Holder` and reached the real fuse spawn on a `-tags fuse` build (unlike `proc`/`mountd` spawn tests, the overlay test binary had no env-var worker dispatch). The Supervisor's ReviveBreaker is per-instance, so it never bounded the multi-process bomb.

**THE RULE (how to apply):** Run tests via **`scripts/test.sh ./...`** (a `ulimit -u` = current-uid-procs + 400 wrapper around `go test`) — both repos, CI included. **Never** run bare `go test` (especially `-tags fuse`/spawn-capable) for fusekit/cc-pool/cc-notes on a machine the user cares about; a git worktree is NOT isolation (shared kernel/process table). Autonomous/workflow test runs use the harness or a disposable VM/container.

**Immediate safety net landed (fusekit + cc-pool, uncommitted on this machine):** `proc/rlimit_darwin.go` `withChildNprocCap` lowers the spawned child's `RLIMIT_NPROC` to current+400 across the fork (darwin only; no-op elsewhere — Linux NPROC counts threads); `scripts/test.sh` in both repos; CI calls it; `overlay/select_test.go testHolderSpec(t)`→`t.TempDir()` and the two FP fall-through tests skip on `fusekit.Built()`. Compile-verified (pure + `-tags fuse`); the harnessed test run was deferred to an isolated/idle moment per the user. **Durable fix = the multi-tenant `fusekit-holder` daemon ([[fusekit-global-holder-direction]]).** The user rejected a `testing.Testing()`-opt-in refusal and `.test`-sniffing as theatre/hacks and a kill-switch script as unneeded — see [[prefers-minimal-fixes-no-guard-layers]]; he wanted generalizable mechanisms (RLIMIT + ulimit harness) and a real root-cause fix. Full forensics: cc-pool cc-notes doc `ef281ea` (`ccn doc show ef281ea`).
